text:
[IMG]
In the circuit shown here, assuming threshold voltage of diode is negligibly small, then voltage $V_{AB}$ is correctly represented by:
options: $V_{AB}$ would be zero at all times.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take $V=V_{0}\sin ωt$ as the potential of the upper source terminal, which is joined to A, relative to the lower terminal, which feeds the anode of the diode; the cathode of the diode is joined to B, and R is connected between A and B.

For $0<ωt<π$ the upper terminal is at the higher potential, so the diode is reverse biased, no current flows through R and $V_{AB}=0$.

For $π<ωt<2π$ the lower terminal is at the higher potential, so the diode is forward biased. With negligible threshold the whole source voltage appears across R, current flowing through R from B to A:

$V_{AB}=V_{0}\sin ωt<0$

So $V_{AB}$ is zero in the first half of every cycle and a negative half-sine loop in the second half. Positive loops, as in option (D), would need the diode connected the other way round.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: A uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T acts perpendicular to a circular copper disc 20 cm in radius. The disc is having a uniform angular velocity of 10 $π$ rad $s^{-1}$ about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to the disc. What is the potential difference developed between the axis of the disc and the rim? $(π=3.14)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the potential difference between the center and the rim of the disc (often called a Faraday disc or unipolar generator), we use the formula for motional EMF in a rotating disc:

$V=\frac{1}{2}BωR^{2}$

where:

$B$ is the magnetic field strength,

$ω$ is the angular velocity,

$R$ is the radius of the disc.

Given:

$B=0.4\text{T}$,

$ω=10π\text{rad/s}$,

$R=20\text{cm}=0.2\text{m}$,

we substitute these values into the formula:

First calculate $R^{2}$:

$R^{2}=(0.2\text{m})^{2}=0.04\text{m}^{2}$

Substitute into the formula:

$V=\frac{1}{2}\times 0.4\times (10π)\times 0.04$

Multiply step-by-step:

$0.4\times 10π=4π$,

Then, $4π\times 0.04=0.16π$,

Finally, multiply by $\frac{1}{2}$: 

$V=\frac{1}{2}\times 0.16π=0.08π$

Substitute $π\approx 3.14$:

$V\approx 0.08\times 3.14=0.2512\text{V}$

Thus, the potential difference developed between the axis and the rim is approximately $0.2512\text{V}$, which corresponds to Option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

The velocity-time graph of an object moving along a straight line is shown in the figure. What is the distance covered by the object between $t=0$ to $t=4s$?

[IMG]

solution.body:
The distance covered is equal to the area under the velocity-time graph from $t=0$ to $t=4s$.

From $t=0$ to $t=2s$, the graph forms a triangle with base $2~s$ and height $10\quad m/s$.

Its area is

$\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 10=10m$

From $t=2s$ to $t=4s$, the graph forms a rectangle with length $2~s$ and height $10\quad m/s$.

Its area is

$2\times 10=20m$

So, total distance

$10+20=30m$

text:
A balloon and its content having mass M is moving up with an acceleration ‘a’. The mass that must be released from the content so that the balloon starts moving up with an acceleration ‘3a’ will be
(Take ‘g’ as acceleration due to gravity)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The upward buoyant force $F$ on the balloon depends only on its volume, so it stays the same when mass is released. With total mass $M$ and upward acceleration $a$:

$F-Mg=Ma\Rightarrow F=M(g+a)$

After a mass $x$ is released, the remaining mass $(M-x)$ accelerates upward at $3a$:

$F-(M-x)g=(M-x)3a\Rightarrow M(g+a)=(M-x)(g+3a)$

$x(g+3a)=M(g+3a)-M(g+a)=2Ma\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2Ma}{3a+g}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The ratio of vapour densities of two gases at the same temperature is $\frac{4}{25}$, then the ratio of r.m.s. velocities will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given that the ratio of the vapour densities of the two gases is 

$\frac{4}{25}.$

Since vapour density is proportional to the molecular mass, we can write

$\frac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}=\frac{4}{25},$

where $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$ are the molecular masses of the gases.

The root mean square (r.m.s.) velocity of a gas is given by

$v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}},$

where:

$R$ is the universal gas constant,

$T$ is the temperature,

$M$ is the molecular mass of the gas.

Since both gases are at the same temperature, the ratio of their r.m.s. velocities is

$\frac{v_{\text{rms,1}}}{v_{\text{rms,2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}}}.$

Substitute the ratio of molecular masses:

$\frac{v_{\text{rms,1}}}{v_{\text{rms,2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{25}{4}}=\frac{5}{2}.$

Thus, the ratio of their r.m.s. velocities is

$\frac{5}{2}.$

The correct answer is Option A: $\frac{5}{2}.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The frequency of revolution of the electron in Bohr's orbit varies with n, the principal quantum number as:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the $n$th Bohr orbit the speed and radius of the electron are

$v_{n}=\dfrac{Ze^{2}}{2ε_{0}hn}\propto \dfrac{1}{n},r_{n}=\dfrac{ε_{0}h^{2}n^{2}}{πmZe^{2}}\propto n^{2}$

The frequency of revolution is the number of turns per second:

$f_{n}=\dfrac{v_{n}}{2πr_{n}}\propto \dfrac{1/n}{n^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{n^{3}}$

The $\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}$ dependence belongs to the energy $E_{n}$, not to the frequency of revolution.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: Earth has mass 8 times and radius 2 times that of a planet. If the escape velocity from the earth is 11.2 km/s, the escape velocity in km/s from the planet will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The escape velocity ($v_{\text{esc}}$) for a planet with mass $M$ and radius $R$ is given by the formula:

$v_{\text{esc}}=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$

where $G$ is the gravitational constant.

For Earth, let's denote its mass as $M_{E}$ and its radius as $R_{E}$. The escape velocity is given as 11.2 km/s. Therefore:

$v_{\text{esc, Earth}}=\sqrt{\frac{2GM_{E}}{R_{E}}}=11.2\text{km/s}$

For the planet in question, its mass $M_{P}$ is $M_{E}/8$ and its radius $R_{P}$ is $R_{E}/2$. The escape velocity from the planet is:

$v_{\text{esc, Planet}}=\sqrt{\frac{2GM_{P}}{R_{P}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2G(M_{E}/8)}{R_{E}/2}}$

Simplifying the expression:

$v_{\text{esc, Planet}}=\sqrt{\frac{2G(M_{E}/8)}{R_{E}/2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2GM_{E}\cdot 2}{8R_{E}}}=\sqrt{\frac{GM_{E}}{2R_{E}}}$

Now, relate it to the escape velocity from Earth:

$v_{\text{esc, Planet}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}\cdot v_{\text{esc, Earth}}$

Calculating further:

$v_{\text{esc, Planet}}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 11.2\text{km/s}=5.6\text{km/s}$

Thus, the escape velocity from the planet is 5.6 km/s. 

Option C: 5.6 km/s is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: Which of the following phenomena cannot be explained by wave theory of light?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Solution Explanation

Among the four listed phenomena:

Reflection of light  

Wave theory (Huygens’s principle, for example) adequately explains reflection.

Refraction of light  

Wave theory also explains refraction via the change of wave speed in different media.

Diffraction of light  

Wave theory (again, Huygens–Fresnel principle) explains the bending of waves around obstacles.

Compton effect  

This involves inelastic scattering of photons by electrons (where the photon loses energy and is scattered with a longer wavelength).  

Wave theory alone cannot explain the discrete energy exchange and wavelength shift; it requires the particle (photon) concept from quantum theory.

Hence, the phenomenon not explained by the (classical) wave theory is the Compton effect.

Answer: (D) Compton effect.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Match List - I with List - II.

  
    List - I
    List - II
  
  
    (A) Angular Impulse
    $(I) M^{0} L^{2} T^{-2}$
  
  
    (B) Latent Heat
    $(II) M L^{2} T^{-3} A^{-1}$
  
  
    (C) Electrical resistivity
    (III$) M L^{2} T^{-1}$
  
  
    (D) Electromotive force
    $(IV) M L^{3} T^{-3} A^{-2}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Angular impulse equals the change in angular momentum, $[τt]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}][\mathrm{T}]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}]$, so (A)–(III).

Latent heat is energy per unit mass, $\dfrac{[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{M}]}=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$, so (B)–(I).

Emf is work per unit charge, $\dfrac{[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{AT}]}=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-1}]$, so (D)–(II).

Resistance $R=\dfrac{V}{I}$ has $[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]$, and resistivity $ρ=\dfrac{RA}{l}$ carries one more power of length: $[ρ]=[\mathrm{ML}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]$, so (C)–(IV).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
[IMG]
A bar magnet has total length $2l=20$ units and the field point P is at a distance $\mathrm{d}=10$ units from the centre of the magnet. If the relative uncertainty of length measurement is $1%$, then uncertainty of the magnetic field at point P is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the uncertainty of the magnetic field at point P, we consider two approaches:

Without considering uncertainty in length $\ell$:

The magnetic field $B$ at point P is given by:

$B=\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{m}{r^{3}}$

Where $B$ is inversely proportional to $r^{3}$:

$B\propto \frac{1}{r^{3}}$

The relative uncertainty in $B$, expressed as a percentage, is calculated by:

$\frac{\Delta B}{B}=3\times \left (\frac{\Delta r}{r}\right )$

Given that the relative uncertainty in length measurement is $1%$, the uncertainty in $B$ becomes:

$%\text{uncertainty in}B=3%$

Method-2: Considering uncertainty in length $\ell$:

Here, we also account for the uncertainty in $\ell$:

$B\propto \frac{1}{r^{3}}$

Thus, the combined relative uncertainty, incorporating $\ell$, is:

$\frac{\Delta B}{B}=\frac{\Delta \ell }{\ell }+3\times \left (\frac{\Delta r}{r}\right )$

Substituting the given uncertainties:

$\frac{\Delta B}{B}=1+3\times 1=4%$

Therefore, the percentage uncertainty in $B$, considering the length $\ell$, is $4%$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The meniscus is convex towards A, so its centre of curvature lies in B. Light from the object in A ($n_{1}=1.3$) refracts into B ($n_{2}=1.4$); taking the direction of the light as positive, $u=-13\text{cm}$ and $R>0$.

Magnification at a single refracting surface:

$m=\dfrac{n_{1}v}{n_{2}u}\Rightarrow -2=\dfrac{1.3v}{1.4\times (-13)}\Rightarrow v=28\text{cm}$

Refraction formula:

$\dfrac{n_{2}}{v}-\dfrac{n_{1}}{u}=\dfrac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{R}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1.4}{28}+\dfrac{1.3}{13}=\dfrac{0.1}{R}$

$0.05+0.1=\dfrac{0.1}{R}\Rightarrow R=\dfrac{0.1}{0.15}=\dfrac{2}{3}\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water?
(Given: density of water $= 1000 kg m^{-3})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, let’s find the weight of the cube and set it equal to the upward buoyant force that keeps the cube floating.

Step 1: Set up the equation for floating

The weight of the cube (mass × gravity) is balanced by the buoyant force (density of water × volume of cube under water × gravity):

$\mathrm{Mg}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}\Rightarrow (400\times 10^{-3})=10^{3}\times \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}$

Step 2: Solve for the volume under water

We find the volume of the cube under water ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}$):

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}=400\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}$

Step 3: Find the total volume of the cube

Each edge of the cube is 10 cm, so total volume is:

$(10\times 10^{-2})^{3}$

Step 4: Find the volume outside water

Subtract the volume under water from the total volume to get the volume outside water:

$(\text{Vol.})_{\text{outside}}=(10\times 10^{-2})^{3}-400\times 10^{-6}$

Calculate the answer:

$=600\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}=600\mathrm{cm}^{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Knowing initial position $\mathrm{x}_{0}$ and initial momentum $p_{0}$ is enough to determine the position and momentum at any time $t$ for a simple harmonic motion with a given angular frequency $ω$.

Reason (R) : The amplitude and phase can be expressed in terms of $\mathrm{x}_{0}$ and $\mathrm{p}_{0}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{A}\sin (ω\mathrm{t}+𝜙) \\ \mathrm{x}_{0}=\mathrm{A}\sin 𝜙\text{.... (1)} \\ \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{mA}ω\cos (ω\mathrm{t}+𝜙) \\ \mathrm{p}_{0}=\mathrm{mA}ω\cos 𝜙\text{.... (2)} \end{array}$

$(1)/(2)\Rightarrow \tan 𝜙=\left (\frac{x_{0}}{p_{0}}\right )mω$

$\sin 𝜙=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}\mathrm{m}ω}{\sqrt{(\mathrm{m}ω\mathrm{x}_{0})^{2}+\mathrm{p}_{0}^{2}}}$

From (1), $A=\frac{x_{0}}{\sin 𝜙}=\frac{\sqrt{(mωx_{0})^{2}+p_{0}^{2}}}{mω}$

This means we can explain assertion with the given reason.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 1 µF is charged to a potential difference of 20 V. The distance between plates is 1 µm. The energy density between plates of capacitor is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The energy density ($u$) between the plates of a capacitor is given by the formula:

$u=\frac{1}{2}ε_{0}E^{2}$

where $ε_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space ($8.85\times 10^{-12}\text{F/m}$) and $E$ is the electric field between the plates. The electric field $E$ is related to the potential difference $V$ and the separation $d$ between the plates by:

$E=\frac{V}{d}$

Given:

Capacitance ($C$) = 1 µF = $1\times 10^{-6}\text{F}$

Potential Difference ($V$) = 20 V

Distance ($d$) = 1 µm = $1\times 10^{-6}\text{m}$

First, calculate the electric field $E$:

$E=\frac{V}{d}=\frac{20\text{V}}{1\times 10^{-6}\text{m}}=2\times 10^{7}\text{V/m}$

Now plug this into the formula for energy density:

$u=\frac{1}{2}\times 8.85\times 10^{-12}\text{F/m}\times (2\times 10^{7}\text{V/m})^{2}$

Calculate $u$:

$u=\frac{1}{2}\times 8.85\times 10^{-12}\times 4\times 10^{14}$

$u=2\times 8.85\times 10^{2}$

$u=1770\text{J/m}^{3}$

This value is approximately $1.8\times 10^{3}\text{J/m}^{3}$. Therefore, the correct option is:

Option A: $1.8\times 10^{3}\text{J/m}^{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: A thin transparent film with refractive index 1.4 , is held on circular ring of radius 1.8 cm . The fluid in the film evaporates such that transmission through the film at wavelength 560 nm goes to a minimum every 12 seconds. Assuming that the film is flat on its two sides, the rate of evaporation is $____________$ $π\times 10^{-13}\mathrm{m}^{3}/\mathrm{s}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a thin film in air, transmitted light is minimum when the film thickness $d$ satisfies $2μd=\left (n-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )λ$. Successive minima therefore differ in thickness by

$\Delta d=\dfrac{λ}{2μ}=\dfrac{560\times 10^{-9}}{2\times 1.4}=2\times 10^{-7}\text{m}$

So every 12 s the thickness falls by $2\times 10^{-7}\text{m}$ over the area of the ring:

$A=πr^{2}=π\left (1.8\times 10^{-2}\right )^{2}=3.24π\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$

Rate of evaporation:

$\dfrac{A\Delta d}{12}=\dfrac{3.24π\times 10^{-4}\times 2\times 10^{-7}}{12}=5.4π\times 10^{-12}=54π\times 10^{-13}\text{m}^{3}\text{s}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 54.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
The volume contraction of a solid copper cube of edge length 10 cm , when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of $7\times 10^{6}\mathrm{Pa}$, would be $__________$ $\mathrm{mm}{}^{3}$.

(Given bulk modulus of copper $=1.4\times 10^{11}\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the volume contraction of the copper cube, we need to use the formula for volumetric strain under pressure, which involves the bulk modulus (K). The volumetric strain is given by the formula:

$\text{Volumetric strain}=\frac{\Delta V}{V}=-\frac{P}{K}$

Where:

$\Delta V$ is the change in volume or volume contraction,

$V$ is the original volume of the cube,

$P$ is the hydraulic pressure applied,

$K$ is the bulk modulus of the material.

Given:

Edge length of the cube, $a=10\text{cm}=0.1\text{m}$

Hydraulic pressure, $P=7\times 10^{6}\text{Pa}$

Bulk modulus of copper, $K=1.4\times 10^{11}\text{Pa}$

Calculate the original volume ($V$) of the cube:
$V=a^{3}=(0.1\text{m})^{3}=0.001\text{m}^{3}$

Calculate the volumetric strain:
$\text{Volumetric strain}=-\frac{P}{K}=-\frac{7\times 10^{6}}{1.4\times 10^{11}}=-5\times 10^{-5}$

Calculate the volume contraction ($\Delta V$):
$\Delta V=V\times \text{Volumetric strain}=0.001\text{m}^{3}\times (-5\times 10^{-5})=-5\times 10^{-8}\text{m}^{3}$

Convert $\Delta V$ from cubic meters to cubic millimeters:
1 cubic meter = $10^{9}$ cubic millimeters. Therefore,

$\Delta V=-5\times 10^{-8}\text{m}^{3}\times 10^{9}\text{mm}^{3}/\text{m}^{3}=-50\text{mm}^{3}$

Thus, the volume contraction of the copper cube, when subjected to the given hydraulic pressure, is $50\quad \text{mm}^{3}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: An electric dipole of dipole moment $6\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{Cm}$ is placed in uniform electric field of magnitude $10^{6}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$. Initially, the dipole moment is parallel to electric field. The work that needs to be done on the dipole to make its dipole moment opposite to the field, will be $_______ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given values:

The dipole moment is $p=6\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{Cm}$.

The electric field is $E=10^{6}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$.

Formula for work done:

Work required to rotate the dipole is 

$W=\Delta U=-pE(\cos θ_{f}-\cos θ_{i})$

where $θ_{i}$ is the initial angle between the dipole and the electric field, and $θ_{f}$ is the final angle.

Angles:

At the start, the dipole is parallel to the field ($θ_{i}=0^{\circ }$), so $\cos θ_{i}=1$.

At the end, the dipole is opposite the field ($θ_{f}=180^{\circ }$), so $\cos θ_{f}=-1$.

Calculation:

$W=-pE(\cos 180^{\circ }-\cos 0^{\circ })=-pE(-1-1)=2pE$

Plug in the values:

$W=2\times (6\times 10^{-6})\times (10^{6})=2\times 6=12\mathrm{J}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift
